title: Red Earth
hero_alt: US-163 toward Monument Valley in the last light
cover_alt: Sunrise over the Bryce Canyon amphitheater
lede: Seven days in the American Southwest, from Route 66 to the Las Vegas sign. Sandstone, straight roads, grazing animals and a lot of alarms before dawn.
meta_description: Seven days in the American Southwest, from the canyons to the Las Vegas sign. Sandstone, straight roads, grazing animals and a lot of alarms before dawn.
intros: We set off from Las Vegas along Route 66, a must, and by the afternoon we reach the South Rim of the Grand Canyon. From the railing the canyon has no scale: only the layers of rock bring some order to the landscape. The first moment of awe of the trip happens right there.

Two faces of the same sandstone: underground, inside the slot of Upper Antelope Canyon, and then high above the Colorado River at Horseshoe Bend, until the last thunderstorm of the evening. Instant Indiana Jones.

US-163 crosses the line between Arizona and Utah and leads straight into the landscape of the western movies: grazing herds, free-roaming horses and the great sandstone buttes still standing where everything else has eroded away. It is the same sky that has been the backdrop for Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner for 77 years.
A night in a dome near Monticello, under a sky full of stars, and an early start, with the telephoto lens ready for whoever lives in the juniper woods.
More than two thousand catalogued stone arches in a single park, and on the horizon the still snow-capped peaks of the La Sal Mountains. In the evening, the road west is a surprise beyond words.
An alarm before dawn to watch the sun spill into the amphitheater, then on foot along the rim and by car along the scenic drive, down to the rock windows further south.
Two nights on a ranch east of Zion, among pastures, old wagons and a herd of bison that lets you come close in the hours of soft light.
Utah’s most visited park, told mostly through its residents: chipmunks, bighorn sheep, deer in the undergrowth. And the river that carved the canyon.
The last day is almost all road. Interstate 15 cuts across the northwest corner of Arizona, enters Nevada and runs all the way to the most famous sign in Las Vegas.

20260405-3W9A6381: In the mid-afternoon the light is harsh and the canyon reads in layers: the terraces in the foreground, the red walls, the North Rim fading into the haze.
20260405-3W9A6401: With the telephoto the canyon compresses: walls, terraces and gorges become a single pattern of horizontal lines.
20260405-3W9A6475: The layers visible from the rim tell almost two billion years of geological history, stacked like the pages of a book.
20260405-3W9A6419: Mules have the right of way.
At the start of the South Kaibab Trail a sign reminds you who is in charge: when the mules go by, follow the wrangler’s instructions.
20260405-3W9A6450: A rock squirrel strikes a pose: photo, right away.
20260405-3W9A6512: A closer portrait: the background melts into the same colors as the canyon.
20260405-3W9A6473: Limestone in the foreground, and behind it the canyon fading into the haze.
20260405-3W9A6590-HDR: At 6:34 pm the low sun lights up only the tops of the terraces. A long, narrow panorama, to hold on to all of the light.
20260406-3W9A6754-HDR: Light pours in through a crack overhead and bounces off walls polished by flash floods. The color changes with every step: orange where the sun hits, violet where it doesn’t reach.
20260406-3W9A6720: Light falls from the slot and grazes the veins of the rock, layer after layer.
20260406-3W9A6794-HDR: The veins in the sandstone are petrified dunes from a desert of some two hundred million years ago.
20260406-3W9A6814-HDR: The cracks overhead light the path; the sand on the floor reflects the light and brightens the walls from below.
20260406-3W9A6861-2: A visitor stops in the only lit spot in the canyon and looks up. In black and white, only the light and the shape of the rock remain.
20260406-3W9A6974-HDR: The Colorado draws its horseshoe about three hundred meters below the rim. The wide-angle lens struggles to take in the whole bend, from the wall in the foreground to the river. Down below, the boats on the water give the bend its scale.
20260406-3W9A6981: Past the bend the river carries on toward the Grand Canyon, with a strip of green along its banks.
20260406-3W9A7060: At 6:54 pm the sun finds a gap beneath the clouds and for a few moments sets the horizon ablaze like a firestorm.
20260407-3W9A7076: On US-163 you cross the state line, and the sign promises “Life Elevated”.
20260407-3W9A7083: For those traveling the other way, a welcome to the Grand Canyon State.
20260407-3W9A7089: Sandstone towers planted in the red sand, under a sky without a cloud too many.
20260407-3W9A7127: A dead trunk in the foreground and, behind it, one of the Mittens, the most recognizable silhouette in the valley.
20260407-3W9A7145: In April the sand is covered with low, dense white and purple flowers. A privilege.
20260407-3W9A7153: Hereford cows graze among the shrubs; in the background the line of mesas runs along the whole horizon.
20260407-3W9A7154: A horse grazes among dry grass and purple flowers. Higher up the slope, small as dots, the others graze too.
20260407-3W9A7168: The slender spire of the Totem Pole with the Yei Bi Chei rocks. Below, the cows rest beside a juniper.
20260407-3W9A7175: At 105 mm the spires stand out from the wall. The thinnest is more than a hundred meters tall.
20260407-3W9A7183: A lone tree between two walls, with the buttes in the distance.
20260407-3W9A7180: The valley floor in the mid-afternoon: sand, shrubs, buttes and a cartoon sky.
20260407-3W9A7364-HDR: Half an hour later, from the same road: the low light warms the grass and the buttes turn lilac.
20260407-3W9A7333-HDR: On US-163, the spot where Forrest stops running. I always wondered how people take these photos: it turns out you have to run too, back and forth between the shoulder and the middle of the road, dodging the passing cars. I spent a few hours there and had a great time.
20260408-3W9A7399: At 6:58 am the first light touches only the white house, in a sea of junipers still in shadow.
20260407-3W9A7388: At 10:32 pm, in the middle of nowhere, the sky fills with stars above the trees lit by the campfire.
20260408-3W9A7575: Early in the morning, among the bushes, a mule deer stops to look before disappearing into the woods.
20260408-3W9A7595: Sandstone walls lined up like the skyscrapers along an avenue.
20260408-3W9A7600: This is Queen Nefertiti Rock: a head of stone poised on a slender neck, recalling the bust of the Egyptian queen.
20260408-3W9A7608: Motionless in the sun, almost the same color as the stone.
20260408-3W9A7604: Stretches of pale sandstone and, at the back, rows of red pinnacles.
20260408-3W9A7610: Balanced Rock and the La Sals.
Balanced Rock, on the left, with the snowy peaks of the La Sal Mountains in the background.
20260408-3W9A7622: The boulder on top weighs more than 3,200 tons and looks as if it had been set there by chance.
20260408-3W9A7624: The La Sal Mountains, rising to nearly 3,900 meters, above the line of red rocks. The contrast is moving.
20260408-3W9A7626: Spires and towers of rock, with the snowy mountains just visible behind them.
20260408-3W9A7627: The tower and its arch, in the Windows section.
20260408-3W9A7628: A bridge of rock seen from below, suspended in the blue.
20260408-3W9A7636: Vertical slabs of sandstone, the “fins”, from which arches form over time.
20260408-3W9A7647: Beneath this valley lies an ancient layer of salt: as it dissolved, the sandstone above it sagged and cracked. Those cracks gave rise to the fins, and then to the arches.
20260408-3W9A7649: The symbol of Utah, small on a horizon of smooth rock.
20260408-3W9A7651: On the way to Bryce, at 7:37 pm, a deer stops on the ridge against the light.
20260408-3W9A7660: Twenty minutes later the sky catches fire behind a row of pines.
20260409-3W9A7813-HDR: At 7:07 am the sun clears the horizon and lights up the hoodoos, the rock spires shaped by freezing and thawing.
20260409-3W9A7816: A few seconds later, the light reaches deeper between the spires.
20260409-3W9A7868: The whole amphitheater in a single glance, at 7:13 am.
20260409-3W9A7892: By mid-morning, the plateaus are visible from the rim all the way to the horizon.
20260409-3W9A8120: A lone hoodoo, with smaller spires lined up behind it.
20260409-3W9A8134: In this part of the park time has already worn the spires away, leaving only slopes of red and white debris.
20260409-3W9A8143: Thousands of hoodoos, packed like the houses of a city seen from above.
20260409-3W9A8148: Further south, along the scenic drive, the walls are pierced by small caves.
20260409-3W9A8157: An arch carved by rain and frost, with the forest showing through.
20260409-3W9A8247: The ranch sign points the way to the horseback rides.
20260409-3W9A8198: Seedlings in pots, waiting for spring to arrive for real.
20260409-3W9A8251: The ranch meadow at 7:33 pm, with an old farm implement abandoned in the grass.
20260410-3W9A8319: At 8 am the bison graze, scattered across the meadow.
20260410-3W9A8337: An old covered wagon, its canvas long gone, rests beside the fence.
20260410-3W9A8525: A bison crosses the meadow while the rest of the herd keeps eating.
20260410-3W9A8531: At 400 mm, a look straight into the lens. The late-afternoon light catches the fur on its back.
20260410-3W9A8624: The sun sinks behind the hills and stretches the shadows across the pasture.
20260410-3W9A8632: From down low, between the blades of grass, the same sun becomes a star.
20260410-3W9A8400: A chipmunk on a sandstone boulder, at 400 mm.
20260410-3W9A8424: Food held tight between its paws, eyes always alert.
20260410-3W9A8472: A desert bighorn sheep on a sandstone ledge. The park reintroduced it in the 1970s.
20260411-3W9A8691: The river that carved Zion’s canyon, green and calm beneath the red walls.
20260411-3W9A8732: A mule deer forages in the undergrowth, almost invisible.
20260411-3W9A8750: On I-15 you re-enter Arizona for less than fifty kilometers, through the Virgin River Gorge.
20260411-3W9A8757: Shortly after, the last state line of the trip.
20260411-3W9A8771: At 6:17 pm, the 1959 sign that marks the arrival in town. End of the trip. Maybe.
